broker_role.title: Your role as a broker
broker_role.summary: What brokers and coordinators do, what they can and cannot change, and how to find your way around the Broker Panel.

broker_what_is_a_broker.title: What is a broker or coordinator?
broker_what_is_a_broker.summary: Brokers and coordinators run the timebank day to day, using a separate part of the site called the Broker Panel.
broker_what_is_a_broker.body:
A broker is the person who runs your timebank day to day. Some communities say "coordinator" instead. Both roles use the same tools in the same way.

A broker helps members swap time fairly and safely. Typical tasks are:

- welcoming new members and approving them when your community checks people before they join
- signing off exchanges that need a broker's approval
- reading messages that have been copied to brokers for safeguarding
- recording your community's vetting decisions
- removing posts, comments and reviews that break the rules
- helping members who find the website hard to use

You do this work in the **Broker Panel**. It is a separate part of the site, built for day-to-day tasks. You still have your own member account as well. You can post listings and swap time like any other member.

## A broker is not a junior admin

A broker and a community admin have different jobs. An admin sets up the community: its settings, its sections and its rules. A broker works inside those rules with members. For that reason brokers are not allowed into the admin panel, and some settings in the Broker Panel are marked **Admin only**.

> The decisions you make in the Broker Panel, such as approvals, reviews and balance changes, are recorded with your name. This keeps a clear record for your community.

broker_can_and_cannot.title: What can a broker do, and what is only for admins?
broker_can_and_cannot.summary: A plain list of the tasks brokers can do, and the ones that need a community admin.
broker_can_and_cannot.body:
Brokers look after members and daily activity. Admins look after the community's setup.

## You can

- approve, suspend and reactivate ordinary members
- edit a member's name, phone, location, tagline and bio
- resend a verification email, send a password reset, or reset two-factor sign-in
- adjust a member's time balance, with a reason
- keep private notes about members
- approve or reject exchanges that need broker approval
- tag listings with a risk level
- review message copies, place members under monitoring and turn off their messaging
- confirm, renew or revoke vetting decisions
- record insurance certificates
- remove posts, comments and reviews that break the rules, and close reports
- change the safeguarding options members can choose
- change the Broker Panel settings that are not marked **Admin only**

## Only an admin can

- change community settings, sections and branding
- give someone a role, such as broker or admin
- create, import, ban or delete accounts
- reactivate a member who was banned (you can lift an ordinary suspension)
- choose the community's safeguarding policy package
- pay hours out of the Community Fund
- set rewards for attending events

## Checks that protect you

To keep things fair, the site stops you acting where you have a personal interest. You cannot:

- approve or reject an exchange you are part of
- moderate content you wrote or are part of
- close a report you made
- adjust your own balance

You also cannot change another broker's or an admin's account. If you try, you will see an error. Ask another broker or an admin to help instead.

broker_becoming_a_broker.title: How does someone become a broker?
broker_becoming_a_broker.summary: A community admin gives the broker role from the admin panel. You then see the Broker Panel link.
broker_becoming_a_broker.body:
Only a community admin can make someone a broker. You cannot ask for the role from your own account.

The admin opens the member's account in the admin panel. They set **Role** to **Broker** and save.

## After you become a broker

1. Sign in as usual.
2. Look at the bar at the top of the page. You now see **Broker Panel**.
3. Press **Broker Panel** to open it.

If you do not see the link, sign out and sign in again. If it is still missing, ask your admin to check your role.

## When the role ends

If you stop being a broker, ask your admin to change your role back to **Member**. The Broker Panel link then disappears. Your notes and decisions stay on record with your name.

> Brokers who are also admins see the admin panel link instead. From inside the Broker Panel, admins also see **Full Admin Panel** at the bottom of the menu.

broker_finding_your_way.title: Finding your way around the Broker Panel
broker_finding_your_way.summary: The menu, the top bar, the search box and the red counters explained.
broker_finding_your_way.body:
The Broker Panel has a menu on the left and a bar along the top. On a phone, press the menu button to open the menu.

## The menu

The menu is grouped by type of work:

- **Dashboard**: what needs your attention now
- **Daily Workflow**: **Members**, **Onboarding**, **Exchanges** and **Messages**
- **Moderation**: **Content Queue**, **Feed Posts**, **Comments**, **Reviews** and **Reports**
- **Compliance & Oversight**: **Safeguarding**, **Safeguarding Options**, **Vetting confirmations**, **User Monitoring**, **Risk Tags** and **Insurance**
- **Records**: **Review Archive**
- **Settings**: **Configuration** and **Help**

Some items only appear if your community uses that section. For example, **Exchanges** only appears when your community uses the exchange workflow.

A red number next to a menu item shows how many things are waiting. The numbers update about once a minute.

## The top bar

- **Back to Site** takes you back to the member side of the site.
- **Search** opens a box where you type a page name, such as "vetting", and jump straight to it. You can also press Ctrl and K together (Cmd and K on a Mac).
- **Help Center** opens the Broker Panel's own guidance page.
- The bell opens your notifications.
- Your name opens a menu with **My Profile** and **Sign Out**.

To make the menu narrower, press **Collapse sidebar** at the top of the menu.

broker_dashboard.title: Using the Broker Dashboard
broker_dashboard.summary: The dashboard shows what is waiting for you, key counts and recent broker activity.
broker_dashboard.body:
The **Broker Dashboard** is the first page you see. It tells you what needs you now.

## What needs you now

At the top, a box lists the kinds of work waiting for review, with the most urgent first. Press any line to go straight to that list. When nothing is waiting you see **All clear**.

## The counters

Below that are counters. Each one opens the matching list, already filtered:

- **Pending Exchanges**: exchanges waiting for broker approval
- **Unreviewed Messages**: message copies nobody has reviewed yet
- **High Risk Listings**: listings tagged high risk
- **Monitored Users**: members under monitoring
- **Vetting review requests**: members who asked for a vetting review
- **Safeguarding Alerts**: urgent safeguarding items
- **Onboarding Flags**: members whose safeguarding choices switch on protections

If a counter shows a dash, it could not load. Press **Refresh** to try again.

## Quick Access and Recent Activity

**Quick Access** has shortcuts to the main tools.

**Recent Activity** lists recent broker actions, such as approvals, message reviews and risk tags. It shows who did what and when. Use it to see what other brokers have already handled, so work is not done twice.

broker_configuration.title: Changing the Broker Panel settings
broker_configuration.summary: Which messages are copied to brokers and how exchange approval works are set in Configuration.
broker_configuration.body:
[Configuration](/broker/configuration) holds the settings for broker work in your community. Settings marked **Admin only** can only be changed by an admin. You can see them, but not change them.

After changing anything, press **Save Changes**. **Unsaved changes** shows until you do.

## Settings brokers can change

These decide which messages are copied to brokers:

- **Copy first contact between members**: copies the first message between any two members.
- **Copy messages from new members**: copies messages from members who joined recently. **New-member monitoring window (days)** sets how long "recently" is.
- **Copy messages on high-risk listings**: copies messages about listings tagged high or critical risk.
- **Random sample percentage**: copies this share of all other messages at random, for spot checks. For example, 5 means about 5 in every 100.
- **Archive retention (days)**: how long reviewed, unflagged message copies are kept before they are deleted.

## Settings only an admin can change

- **Copy all messages to broker**: copies every message between members.
- **Broker approval required**: exchanges wait for a broker's approval.
- **Auto-approve low-risk exchanges**: lets most exchanges go ahead without a broker.
- **Max hours without approval**: with auto-approve on, exchanges above this many hours still need a broker.
- **Insurance tracking enabled**: lets members add insurance records in their settings.

## Choosing settings

Copying more messages gives brokers more to read. It also reaches further into members' privacy. Agree the settings with your admin and safeguarding lead. Choose the lightest settings that keep people safe.

> This guide describes the settings that change how the site behaves. If you are unsure what a setting does, ask your admin before changing it.

broker_members.title: Looking after members
broker_members.summary: Approve new members, keep notes, help people with their accounts and correct balances.

broker_approve_new_members.title: How do I approve a new member?
broker_approve_new_members.summary: New registrations wait in the Pending tab until a broker or admin approves them.
broker_approve_new_members.body:
If your community checks people before they can take part, each new registration waits for approval. You approve them from **Members** or **Onboarding**.

1. Open [Members](/broker/members).
2. Press the **Pending** tab. The red number on **Members** in the menu shows how many are waiting.
3. Find the person. Press the three-dot menu at the end of their row and choose **View details** to check their details first.
4. Press the three-dot menu again and choose **Approve**.
5. Press **Approve** again to confirm.

The member can now sign in and use the site. They get a welcome email and a notification. If your community gives new members starting hours, these are added when you approve them.

## Approving several people at once

1. On the **Pending** tab, tick the box next to each person.
2. Press **Approve selected**.

Use this only when you have already checked each person.

## If you do not want to approve someone

There is no reject button in the Broker Panel. Leave the person pending and talk to your admin or your community's lead about what to do. Do not approve someone to "sort it out later".

> The [Onboarding](/broker/onboarding) page has the same pending list under **Pending Approvals**, with an **Approve** option in each row's menu.

broker_members_list.title: Finding and filtering members
broker_members_list.summary: Search the member list and use tabs to find people who are pending, suspended or have never signed in.
broker_members_list.body:
[Members](/broker/members) lists everyone in your community. Across the top you see **Total members**, **Pending approval**, **Active members** and **Suspended members**. Press a counter to open that list.

## Tabs

- **All**: everyone
- **Pending**: waiting for approval
- **Active**: approved members who can use the site
- **Suspended**: members who cannot sign in at the moment
- **Never logged in**: approved members who have not signed in yet
- **Onboarding incomplete**: members who have not finished the setup steps

The last two tabs are a good place to start when you want to offer help to people who are stuck.

## Searching and filtering

- Type a name or email into **Search members...**.
- Use **Filter by role** to show only members, brokers or admins, for example.

## What each row shows

Each row shows the member's name, status, role, whether their email is verified, their balance in hours, when they were last active and when they joined.

## Row actions

Press the three-dot menu at the end of a row to:

- **View details**: open the member's full record
- **View Profile**: see their public profile in a new tab
- **Send Message**: start a message to them in a new tab
- **Notes**: read or add private notes
- **Check Vetting**: open their vetting record
- **Approve**, **Suspend** or **Reactivate**, depending on their status

broker_member_details.title: Viewing a member's full record
broker_member_details.summary: The member record brings together their status, balance, compliance records, notes and account actions.
broker_member_details.body:
Open a member's record to see everything about them in one place.

1. Open [Members](/broker/members).
2. Press the three-dot menu on their row.
3. Choose **View details**.

At the top you see their name, status, role, email address and whether the email is verified.

## Tabs in the record

- **Overview**: their balance, when they joined, when they were last active, and whether they finished onboarding. A **Membership journey** line shows when they registered, verified their email and were approved.
- **Compliance**: their **Contact attestation** (vetting decision), any **Insurance certificates** and any **Consents** they have given.
- **Notes**: private notes from brokers and admins.
- **Actions**: account tools, such as approving, suspending, sending a password reset or adjusting their balance. You can also edit parts of their profile here.

## Editing a profile

On the **Actions** tab, press **Edit** next to **Profile**. You can change **First name**, **Last name**, **Phone**, **Location**, **Tagline** and **Bio**. Press **Save changes**.

You cannot change a member's email address, role or status here. Ask an admin if one of these needs to change.

> Only change a member's profile when they ask you to, or when it breaks your community's rules. Tell them what you changed.

broker_member_notes.title: Keeping private notes about a member
broker_member_notes.summary: Notes help brokers share context. Members cannot see them.
broker_member_notes.body:
Notes let brokers and admins keep a shared record about a member. Members never see these notes.

## Adding a note

1. Open [Members](/broker/members).
2. Press the notes button on the member's row, or choose **Notes** from the three-dot menu. You can also use the **Notes** tab in the member's record.
3. Choose a **Category**: **General**, **Outreach**, **Support**, **Onboarding**, **Concern** or **Follow up**.
4. Type your note in the box.
5. Press the send button.

Each note shows who wrote it and when.

## Managing notes

- **Pin note** keeps an important note at the top.
- **Edit note** lets you correct a note.
- **Delete note** removes it.

## What to write

Write facts, not opinions. Good notes are short and useful to the next broker, for example: "Called 3 May. Prefers phone to email. Wants help finding gardening work."

> Do not record vetting certificates, health details or other sensitive information in notes unless your community's rules say you may. A member can ask to see the information you hold about them.

broker_suspend_member.title: Suspending or reactivating a member
broker_suspend_member.summary: Suspending stops a member signing in. You can reactivate them later.
broker_suspend_member.body:
Suspending a member stops them signing in and taking part. It is reversible.

## Suspending

1. Open [Members](/broker/members) and find the member.
2. Press the three-dot menu on their row and choose **Suspend**.
3. Read the message and press **Suspend** to confirm.

The member gets a notification. Write a note on their record explaining why, so other brokers understand.

## Suspending several members

Tick the box next to each person and press **Suspend selected**.

## Reactivating

1. Press the **Suspended** tab.
2. Press the three-dot menu on the member's row and choose **Reactivate**.

The member can sign in again and is told their account is active. Press **Reactivate** only once: each press sends them another message.

## Limits

- You can only suspend and reactivate ordinary members. You cannot change another broker's or an admin's account.
- If an admin banned a member, only an admin can reactivate them.

> Suspension is a serious step. For a safeguarding concern, follow your community's safeguarding process first. You may only need to turn off the member's messaging, which you can do from **User Monitoring**.

broker_account_help.title: Helping a member who cannot get into their account
broker_account_help.summary: Resend a verification email, send a password reset, or reset two-factor sign-in for a member.
broker_account_help.body:
Many requests for help are about signing in. You can fix most of them from the member's record.

1. Open [Members](/broker/members).
2. Press the three-dot menu on the member's row and choose **View details**.
3. Open the **Actions** tab.

## "I never got the email to confirm my address"

Press **Resend verification**. Ask the member to check their spam or junk folder too.

## "I forgot my password"

Press **Send password reset**. The member gets an email with a link to choose a new password. You never see or set their password.

## "I lost the phone I use for two-factor sign-in"

Two-factor sign-in asks for a code from a phone app as well as a password.

1. First, make sure the person asking really is the account holder. Follow your community's process for this.
2. In the box above the button, write an incident reference and how you checked their identity. You need at least 10 characters.
3. Press **Reset 2FA**.

The member is signed out everywhere and told by email and notification. They can then sign in with their password and set up two-factor again.

> To reset two-factor sign-in, you must have signed in with two-factor yourself within the last few minutes. If you see an error, sign out, sign in again and retry straight away.

broker_adjust_balance.title: How do I correct a member's time balance?
broker_adjust_balance.summary: Add or remove hours from a member's balance, with a reason the member can see.
broker_adjust_balance.body:
You can add hours to a member's balance or take hours away. Use this to correct a mistake, not as a normal way to pay someone.

1. Open [Members](/broker/members).
2. Press the three-dot menu on the member's row and choose **View details**.
3. Open the **Actions** tab and press **Adjust balance**.
4. In **Amount (hours)**, type a positive number to add hours, or a negative number to remove hours. For example, type 2 to add two hours or -1.5 to remove one and a half.
5. In **Reason**, explain why. This is required.
6. Press **Apply adjustment**.

## What the member sees

The adjustment appears in the member's wallet as a separate entry. It shows your reason and "Admin" as the other party. The member also gets a notification.

## Limits

- A balance cannot go below zero.
- You cannot adjust your own balance. Ask another broker or an admin.
- The change is recorded with your name, the reason and the balance before and after.

## Correcting an exchange

If hours were recorded wrongly in a completed exchange, the Broker Panel cannot undo that exchange. The only fix available to you is to adjust each member's balance separately. Agree the correction with both members first. Mention the exchange in each reason so the history makes sense.

> Adding hours creates new hours in your community. Follow your community's rules on when this is allowed.

broker_supporting_members.title: Supporting members who find technology hard
broker_supporting_members.summary: Practical ways to help members who struggle with the website, and what the site does not let you do for them.
broker_supporting_members.body:
Some members find websites confusing or stressful. You can make a big difference by being patient and practical.

## Ways to help

- Use the **Never logged in** and **Onboarding incomplete** tabs in [Members](/broker/members) to find people who may be stuck. Offer a phone call.
- Sit with the member, or talk them through each step on the phone. Let them press the buttons themselves where they can.
- Send a password reset or a verification email for them from their record.
- With their permission, correct small mistakes in their profile, such as a spelling error in their name.
- Suggest the accessible version of the site if your community offers one. It is simpler and works well with screen readers.
- Write a note on their record about what helps them, such as "prefers phone calls".

## What you cannot do for them

The Broker Panel does not let you post listings, send messages or record exchanges as if you were the member. Every action a member takes must come from their own account.

Never ask for a member's password, and never sign in as them.

## Family members and carers

A member can link their account with a family member or carer they trust. The member does this themselves from the **Linked** tab in their **Settings**. The linked person can then help in the ways the member agrees to. This is the member's choice. Brokers cannot set it up for them.

broker_exchanges.title: Exchanges and listings
broker_exchanges.summary: Approve exchanges that need a broker, deal with problems, and tag listings that need extra care.

broker_exchange_when_approval.title: When does an exchange need a broker's approval?
broker_exchange_when_approval.summary: Which exchanges wait for a broker, and what members see while they wait.
broker_exchange_when_approval.body:
An exchange is an agreement between two members to swap time. In some communities a broker must approve an exchange before it can go ahead.

## How it works

1. A member asks to swap time with another member, usually from a listing.
2. The other member accepts.
3. At that point the site checks whether a broker needs to approve it.
4. If so, the exchange waits in [Exchanges](/broker/exchanges) with the status **Pending Broker Approval**. Brokers and admins get a notification.

## What decides it

- **Safeguarding.** If either member chose a safeguarding option that needs broker approval, their exchanges always wait for a broker.
- **Your community's rules.** An admin can turn on **Broker approval required** in [Configuration](/broker/configuration). With only that setting on, every exchange waits for a broker.
- **Low-risk exchanges.** If an admin also turns on **Auto-approve low-risk exchanges**, most exchanges go ahead without a broker.

Even with auto-approve on, a broker is still needed when:

- the listing has a **High** or **Critical** risk tag
- the listing's risk tag says **Broker approval required**
- the hours are above **Max hours without approval**

## What members see

While they wait, both members see that the exchange is waiting for a broker. Nothing else happens until a broker approves or rejects it. Please deal with waiting exchanges promptly, because the members cannot start until you do.

broker_approve_exchange.title: How do I approve or reject an exchange?
broker_approve_exchange.summary: Check an exchange that is waiting for a broker, then approve it or reject it with a reason.
broker_approve_exchange.body:
Exchanges waiting for you appear under the **Pending** tab in **Exchanges**.

1. Open [Exchanges](/broker/exchanges). The counter **Pending broker review** shows how many are waiting.
2. Press the **Pending** tab.
3. Press the view button on a row to open the exchange. Check who the **Requester** and **Provider** are, the listing, and any **Risk Tag**.
4. Press **Approve** or **Reject**.

## Approving

Add a note in **Notes (optional)** if it helps, for example "Please meet in a public place for the first session". Press **Approve** to confirm.

Both members are told the exchange is approved and they can begin. Your note appears on their exchange page as **Broker Notes**.

## Rejecting

You must give a reason in **Reason (required)**. Press **Reject** to confirm.

The exchange is cancelled. Both members get a notification that includes your reason. Your reason also appears on their exchange page. Write it kindly and plainly.

## Things to know

- You cannot approve or reject an exchange you are part of. Another broker must do it.
- You cannot change the hours or add conditions when you approve. If something needs to change, reject it with a clear reason, or talk to the members before approving.

> Before you approve, it helps to look at both members' records and any safeguarding choices they made.

broker_exchange_list.title: Understanding the Exchanges list
broker_exchange_list.summary: What each tab and status means, and what the exchange detail page shows.
broker_exchange_list.body:
[Exchanges](/broker/exchanges) lists the exchanges in your community. Use the tabs to filter them:

- **All**: every exchange
- **Pending**: waiting for a broker's approval
- **Approved**: approved and ready to start
- **In Progress**: the members are doing the work
- **Completed**: finished and the hours have moved
- **Cancelled**: stopped, or rejected by a broker
- **Disputed**: the members disagree

Each row shows the two members, the listing, the status, the hours and the date. The hours appear once the members have confirmed them.

## The exchange page

Press the view button on a row to open the exchange. It shows:

- **Exchange progress**: where the exchange has got to
- the **Requester** (the member asking for help) and the **Provider** (the member giving time)
- any **Risk Tag** on the listing, and whether it needs **Broker approval required** or **Insurance required**
- **Broker Notes** from the broker who decided on it
- **History**: each step, such as **Request created**, **Provider confirmed hours** and **Requester confirmed hours**, with who did it and when

Press **Back to Exchanges** to return to the list.

broker_exchange_problems.title: What can I do when an exchange goes wrong?
broker_exchange_problems.summary: How disputes happen, what the Broker Panel can and cannot do about them, and how to correct mistakes.
broker_exchange_problems.body:
Sometimes members disagree about an exchange, or hours are recorded wrongly. Here is what the Broker Panel can do today.

## Disputed exchanges

An exchange becomes **Disputed** when:

- the two members confirm very different hours, or
- a member reports a problem, such as the other person not turning up.

The members are told a broker will review it. You can see these exchanges under the **Disputed** tab in [Exchanges](/broker/exchanges).

The Broker Panel has no button to settle a dispute. While an exchange is disputed, no hours move.

## What to do

1. Open the exchange and read its **History**.
2. Contact both members. Listen to each side.
3. Agree a fair outcome with them. Write a note on each member's record.
4. If hours should move, use **Adjust balance** on each member's record. Add hours to one and remove the same hours from the other. Mention the exchange in each reason.
5. If the dispute is about behaviour or safety, follow your community's safeguarding process.

## A completed exchange with the wrong hours

The Broker Panel cannot undo a completed exchange. Use **Adjust balance** on both members in the same way, after agreeing it with them.

> Keep corrections rare, fair and explained. Members can see each adjustment and its reason in their wallet.

broker_risk_tags.title: Tagging a listing that needs extra care
broker_risk_tags.summary: Risk tags mark listings to watch, and can require broker approval or insurance for exchanges.
broker_risk_tags.body:
A risk tag marks a listing that needs extra care, for example work at height or help with money. The tag is on the listing, not on the member.

## Tagging a listing

1. Open [Risk Tags](/broker/risk-tags).
2. Press **Tag Listing**.
3. In **Search Listing**, type part of the listing title and choose it.
4. Choose a **Risk Level**: **Low**, **Medium**, **High** or **Critical**.
5. Choose a **Risk Category**, such as **Safeguarding**, **Financial**, **Health & Safety**, **Legal**, **Reputation** or **Potential Fraud**.
6. Add **Internal Notes** for other brokers if useful.
7. Turn on **Broker approval required** if exchanges for this listing should wait for a broker.
8. Turn on **Insurance required** if the member giving time must have insurance on record.
9. Press **Create Tag**.

Brokers and admins are notified when a listing is tagged **High** or **Critical**.

## What a tag changes

- If your community uses **Auto-approve low-risk exchanges**, listings tagged **High** or **Critical** still need a broker's approval.
- If your community copies messages about high-risk listings, messages about **High** and **Critical** listings are copied to brokers.

## Changing or removing a tag

The tabs filter tags by level. Use the edit button on a row to change a tag and press **Update Tag**. Use the remove button to delete it.

broker_insurance.title: Recording insurance certificates
broker_insurance.summary: Add, check, verify or reject members' insurance records.
broker_insurance.body:
Some activities need the member giving time to have insurance. [Insurance](/broker/insurance) keeps a record of members' insurance.

If your community tracks insurance, members can add their own insurance details from the **Privacy** tab in their **Settings**. These arrive here for you to check.

## Adding a certificate for a member

1. Press **Add Certificate**.
2. Use **Search Member** to find the member.
3. Choose the **Insurance Type**, such as **Public Liability** or **Professional Indemnity**.
4. Fill in **Provider Name**, **Policy Number**, **Coverage Amount**, **Start Date** and **Expiry Date**.
5. Press **Add Certificate**.

## Checking a certificate

- Use the tabs to see **Pending**, **Submitted**, **Verified**, **Expiring Soon**, **Expired** and **Rejected** certificates.
- Press the view button to see the details. If a file is attached, press **View Certificate File**.
- Press the verify button when you have checked it.
- Press the reject button if it is not acceptable, and give a reason.
- Press the delete button to remove a record you added in error.

## Why it matters

If a listing's risk tag says **Insurance required**, the member giving time needs a verified insurance certificate that has not expired. Without one, the exchange cannot go ahead.

> Follow your community's rules on what counts as acceptable insurance. Do not collect more personal information than you need.

broker_safeguarding.title: Safeguarding
broker_safeguarding.summary: Members' safeguarding choices, message review, monitoring, vetting decisions and what to do when you are worried.

broker_safeguarding_overview.title: How safeguarding works in the Broker Panel
broker_safeguarding_overview.summary: An overview of the safeguarding tools brokers use, and how they fit together.
broker_safeguarding_overview.body:
Safeguarding means protecting members from harm, especially members who may be at risk. The Broker Panel gives you several tools for this. Each one has its own article.

- **Members' safeguarding choices.** When they join, members can say they need extra support. Their choices can limit who contacts them or send their exchanges to a broker.
- **Coordinator help requests.** When a member cannot message someone who is protected, they can ask a coordinator to help. You get a notification.
- **Message review.** Some messages are copied to brokers to read, depending on your community's settings. You review them in **Messages**.
- **User monitoring.** You can place a member under monitoring, so their messages are copied to brokers. You can also turn off their messaging.
- **Vetting confirmations.** You record whether your community has completed its safety checks on a member. Some protected members can only be contacted by vetted members.
- **Safeguarding Options.** You can change the list of choices members see when they join.

## Your community's process comes first

These tools support your community's safeguarding process. They do not replace it. Your community should have a named safeguarding lead. Know who that person is and how to reach them.

> If someone is in immediate danger, contact the emergency services first. Then tell your safeguarding lead.

broker_member_safeguarding_choices.title: What happens when a member chooses a safeguarding option?
broker_member_safeguarding_choices.summary: Each safeguarding option can switch on protections. Here is what each one does.
broker_member_safeguarding_choices.body:
When members join, your community can ask if they need extra support. They tick options such as needing a coordinator to arrange their exchanges. Each option can switch on one or more protections, called triggers.

## What each trigger does

- **Monitor messaging**: other members cannot message this member directly. Anyone who tries is offered **Request coordinator help** instead. The member is also left out of suggested matches.
- **Require coordinator approval**: any exchange this member takes part in waits for a broker's approval.
- **Vetted members only**: only members with a confirmed vetting decision can contact this member. It needs your community's safeguarding policy to be set up.
- **Notify safeguarding staff**: brokers and admins get a notification when a member ticks the option while joining.

If a member ticks several options, all their triggers apply together.

## Changing their mind

Members can see and revoke their choices from the **Safeguarding & support** tab in their **Settings**. When they revoke a choice, brokers and admins are notified. Its protections stop unless another option they chose still applies them.

## Seeing members' choices

The **Onboarding Flags** counter on the [Broker Dashboard](/broker) shows how many members have active safeguarding choices that switch on protections.

> Treat these choices as private. Only other brokers and admins should know about them. Never mention them to other members.

broker_safeguarding_options.title: Changing the safeguarding options members can choose
broker_safeguarding_options.summary: Add, edit or switch off the safeguarding options members see when they join.
broker_safeguarding_options.body:
[Safeguarding Options](/broker/safeguarding-options) is the list of choices members see when they join. Brokers and admins can change it.

The page shows **Active Options** that members can choose, and **Inactive Options** that have been switched off.

## Adding an option

1. Press **Add Option**.
2. Fill in **Option Key**. This is a short internal name with no spaces, such as needs_coordinator. Members do not see it.
3. Fill in **Display Label**. This is the sentence members tick, for example "I would like a coordinator to help arrange my exchanges".
4. Add **Description Help** to explain the option in plain words. Add a **Help URL** if your community has a page about it.
5. Choose **Checkbox** as the **Option Type** for a simple tick box, or **Info** for text only.
6. Turn on **Required** only if every member must answer it.
7. Under **Behavioral Triggers**, turn on the protections this option should switch on.
8. Press **Create Option**.

## Editing or switching off an option

- Press the edit button on an option, make your changes and press **Save Changes**.
- Press the switch-off button and confirm with **Deactivate**. Members can no longer choose it.

You cannot switch off an option that members have chosen if it protects them. This keeps their protections in place.

> Changing options affects vulnerable people. Agree changes with your safeguarding lead first. Keep the wording short, kind and clear.

broker_coordinator_help.title: When a member asks for coordinator help
broker_coordinator_help.summary: What to do when a member cannot message a protected member and asks a coordinator to help.
broker_coordinator_help.body:
Some members have asked not to be contacted directly. If another member tries to message them, the site stops the message. It offers a **Request coordinator help** button instead.

When the member presses it, brokers and admins get a notification and an email. It says something like "Coordinator help requested", with the name of the person asking and the person they want to reach.

## What to do

1. Read the notification. Note who is asking and who they want to contact.
2. Open the protected member's record in [Members](/broker/members). Read their notes.
3. Contact the protected member in the way your community's process sets out, for example by phone. Ask if they are happy to be put in touch.
4. If they agree, arrange the contact safely. For example, you could set up a first meeting with a broker present.
5. If they do not agree, tell the person who asked, kindly and without giving reasons.
6. Write a note on both members' records about what you did.

## Things to know

- The Broker Panel does not keep a list of these requests. The notification and email are your record, so act on them promptly.
- The protected member's safety comes first. Never share their contact details without their agreement.

> A member may also be blocked because the person they want to reach only accepts contact from vetted members. They may then ask for a vetting review, which you handle in **Vetting confirmations**.

broker_message_review.title: Why are messages copied to brokers?
broker_message_review.summary: Which messages are copied for review, what you can see, and what members are told.
broker_message_review.body:
Your community can copy some members' messages to brokers so you can check that people are safe. The message is still delivered normally. The copy goes to [Messages](/broker/messages) for review.

## Why a message is copied

Each copy shows a **Copy Reason**:

- **First Contact**: the first message between two members
- **New Member**: a message from someone who joined recently
- **High Risk Listing**: a message about a listing tagged high or critical risk
- **Flagged User**: a message to or from a member under monitoring
- **Random Sample**: a message chosen at random for spot checks

Which of these apply depends on the settings in [Configuration](/broker/configuration).

## What you can see

When you open a copied message, you see the message and the conversation between the two members around it. This can include earlier messages that were not copied. For a group conversation, you see the group's messages.

## What members are told

When message copying is switched on, members see a notice in their conversations. It says messages may be reviewed by a coordinator for safeguarding.

## Your responsibility

- Read only what you need to make a decision.
- Never share what you read, except with your safeguarding lead or when the law requires it.
- Your review decisions are recorded with your name.

broker_review_message.title: How do I review a copied message?
broker_review_message.summary: Mark a message as reviewed, flag a concern, or approve and archive it.
broker_review_message.body:
Message copies waiting for review are under the **Unreviewed** tab in **Messages**. The red number on **Messages** in the menu shows how many are waiting.

1. Open [Messages](/broker/messages).
2. Press the **Unreviewed** tab.
3. Press the eye button on a row for a quick look, or open the message to see the whole conversation.
4. Choose what to do.

## Your choices

- **Mark Reviewed** (or **Review** in the list): you have read it and there is no concern. In the quick view you can add **Review Notes** first.
- **Flag**: you have a concern. Choose a **Severity** (**Info**, **Warning**, **Concern** or **Urgent**) and describe the concern in **Flag Reason**. A reason is required.
- **Approve & Archive**: on the message page, this saves a permanent, read-only copy of the record in the **Review Archive**. You can add **Decision Notes**. Once archived, the record cannot be changed.

## Tabs

- **Unreviewed**: waiting for a broker
- **Flagged**: messages a broker has flagged
- **Reviewed**: messages already reviewed
- **All**: everything

## After you flag a message

Flagging records your concern. It does not stop the member or warn anyone by itself. Decide what else is needed. You might place the member under monitoring, turn off their messaging, or contact your safeguarding lead.

> Do not tell the member you have flagged their message unless your safeguarding lead agrees.

broker_review_archive.title: Using the Review Archive
broker_review_archive.summary: The Review Archive keeps permanent, read-only records of message reviews.
broker_review_archive.body:
The [Review Archive](/broker/archives) keeps a permanent record of message copies that a broker approved and archived. Records here cannot be edited.

## Finding a record

- Use the tabs: **All**, **Approved** or **Flagged**.
- Type in **Search archive...** to search.

Each row shows the sender, receiver, listing, **Copy Reason**, **Decision**, who decided and when.

## Opening a record

Press a row to open it. You see:

- **Target Message**: the message that was copied
- **Decision**: what was decided, by whom, and any **Decision Notes**
- **Conversation Snapshot**: the conversation as it was when the decision was made

A note at the top reminds you the record is preserved exactly as it was reviewed.

## Why it matters

The archive shows what your community knew and when it acted. It can support a safeguarding investigation. It also shows that reviews happened.

> Records in the archive are kept. Message copies in **Messages** are different: once reviewed, unflagged copies are deleted after the number of days in **Archive retention (days)** in [Configuration](/broker/configuration). Flagged copies are kept longer.

broker_user_monitoring.title: Placing a member under monitoring
broker_user_monitoring.summary: Copy a member's messages to brokers for a set time, and turn off their messaging if needed.
broker_user_monitoring.body:
Monitoring copies every message a member sends or receives to brokers for review. Use it when you have a concern about a member.

## Adding a member

1. Open [User Monitoring](/broker/monitoring).
2. Press **Add User**.
3. In **Search User**, type a name or email and choose the member.
4. In **Reason**, explain why. This is required. Future brokers will read it.
5. Choose a **Duration**: 7, 14, 30, 60 or 90 days. Monitoring then ends by itself.
6. If the member should not send messages at all for now, turn on **Disable messaging while monitored**.
7. Press **Add User**.

## What happens

- The member gets a notification that their account is under review. If you turned off messaging, it says their messaging is restricted.
- Copies of their messages arrive in [Messages](/broker/messages) with the reason **Flagged User**. Brokers and admins get a notification for each copy.
- With messaging turned off, the member cannot send messages. They can still receive them.

## Changing or ending monitoring

- Press the edit button on the row to change the reason, duration or messaging setting, then press **Save Changes**.
- Press the remove button and confirm with **Remove** to end monitoring. The member is told their restrictions have been lifted.

The counter **Expiring within 7 days** shows who will come off monitoring soon.

> Monitoring is a serious step that affects a member's privacy. Keep it as short as possible, record why, and review it before it ends.

broker_vetting_confirm.title: How do I record a vetting decision?
broker_vetting_confirm.summary: Record that your community has completed its safety checks on a member, without storing any documents.
broker_vetting_confirm.body:
Vetting means the safety checks your community carries out before someone works with people who may be at risk. [Vetting confirmations](/broker/vetting) records your community's decision only. It never stores certificates or check results.

## Before you start

The **Safeguarding contact policy** box at the top shows your community's policy package and the confirmation it needs. An admin chooses the policy package. Until they do, you cannot record decisions, and you will see a message saying so.

## Confirming a member

1. Find the member. Use the search box or the **Confirmation status** filter.
2. Press **Confirm attestation**. An attestation is a formal statement that the checks were done.
3. Under **Underlying certification scheme(s)**, choose the checks your community completed.
4. In **Certified scope**, describe exactly what the decision covers, for example "befriending adults".
5. Add **Private broker notes** if needed. Do not enter certificate numbers or check results.
6. Set **Community review due**. After this date the confirmation stops counting until someone renews it.
7. Fill in **Authority membership expiry** if the scheme has one.
8. Tick the box to confirm the checks were done.
9. Press **Confirm safeguarding certification**.

## Renewing

When a confirmation has expired, the button says **Renew confirmation**. Follow the same steps.

## Why it matters

Some protected members only accept contact from vetted members. A member needs a confirmed, in-date decision to contact them.

> Never ask a member to send you a vetting document through messages, and never upload one. The checks themselves stay in your community's own process, outside this site.

broker_vetting_revoke_review.title: Revoking a vetting decision or answering a review request
broker_vetting_revoke_review.summary: Withdraw a vetting confirmation, or close a member's request for a vetting review.
broker_vetting_revoke_review.body:
## Revoking a confirmation

Revoke a confirmation when it should no longer count, for example after a concern.

1. Open [Vetting confirmations](/broker/vetting) and find the member.
2. Press **Revoke attestation**.
3. Choose a **Revocation reason**: **Community decision withdrawn**, **Member requested a correction**, **Safeguarding policy changed** or **Recorded in error**.
4. Press **Revoke confirmation**.

The change applies straight away. The member can no longer contact protected members who only accept vetted contact.

## Review requests

A member can ask for a vetting review from the **Safeguarding & support** tab in their **Settings**. This often happens when they are blocked from contacting someone.

1. Press the **Review requests** counter, or choose **Review requested** in the **Confirmation status** filter.
2. If your community has completed its checks, press **Confirm attestation** and record the decision.
3. If not, press **Resolve request**. Choose a **Review outcome**: **No change**, **Duplicate request** or **Member contacted**. Then press **Resolve request** again to confirm.

## Viewing details

Press **View details** to see the schemes, scope, private notes and dates for a member's current decision.

> Every decision is recorded with your name and the reason. Take care, because these decisions control who can contact protected members.

broker_safeguarding_page.title: What is on the Safeguarding page?
broker_safeguarding_page.summary: The Safeguarding page gathers flagged messages, guardian arrangements and members' choices. It needs extra access.
broker_safeguarding_page.body:
The [Safeguarding](/broker/safeguarding) page brings together safeguarding records in one place. Its tabs are:

- **Flagged Messages**: message copies for safeguarding review
- **Guardian Assignments**: records of guardian arrangements staff have made for members who want extra support
- **Member Preferences**: the safeguarding choices members have made
- **Support Actions**: actions prepared on a member's behalf that are waiting for their approval

## Access

This page needs special safeguarding access, on top of the broker role. Without it the page looks empty, even when there are records. If you need this page for your work, ask your admin.

Even with access, some actions on this page are only for admins or named safeguarding staff. These include creating guardian arrangements and recording approvals.

## Where brokers do most of the work

Most day-to-day safeguarding tasks happen on other pages that every broker can use:

- [Messages](/broker/messages) for reviewing copied messages
- [User Monitoring](/broker/monitoring) for monitoring members and turning off messaging
- [Vetting confirmations](/broker/vetting) for vetting decisions
- [Safeguarding Options](/broker/safeguarding-options) for the choices members see

broker_worried_about_member.title: What should I do if I am worried about a member?
broker_worried_about_member.summary: Steps to take when you have a safeguarding concern, and the tools that can help.
broker_worried_about_member.body:
If you are worried that a member is being harmed, or may harm someone, act promptly and calmly.

## If someone is in immediate danger

Contact the emergency services straight away. Then tell your safeguarding lead.

## Otherwise

1. **Write down what you know.** Stick to facts: what you saw or were told, when, and by whom. Add a note with the category **Concern** on the member's record.
2. **Tell your safeguarding lead.** They decide what happens next, including whether to involve outside agencies.
3. **Do not investigate alone.** Do not question the people involved in detail unless your lead asks you to.
4. **Do not warn the person you are worried about.** It could put someone at risk.
5. **Do not delete anything.** Messages, notes and records may be needed as evidence.

## Tools that can help while your lead decides

- Place the member under monitoring, and turn off their messaging if needed, in [User Monitoring](/broker/monitoring).
- Reject exchanges that are waiting for approval, with a neutral reason.
- Tag a listing that worries you in [Risk Tags](/broker/risk-tags).
- Revoke a vetting confirmation in [Vetting confirmations](/broker/vetting).
- Suspend the member in [Members](/broker/members) if your lead agrees.

## Look after yourself

Safeguarding concerns can be upsetting. Talk to your safeguarding lead or another broker about how you feel.

broker_moderation.title: Moderating content
broker_moderation.summary: Check content waiting for review, remove posts, comments and reviews, and deal with members' reports.

broker_content_queue.title: Using the Content Queue
broker_content_queue.summary: Posts that look like spam are held back for review. Approve them or reject them with a reason.
broker_content_queue.body:
The [Content Queue](/broker/moderation/queue) holds content that is waiting for a moderator before members can see it.

## What arrives here

- **Posts that look like spam.** The site hides a post automatically if it looks like spam, for example very long links or lots of capital letters. These posts arrive with the status **Flagged**.
- **Events waiting for review.** If your community reviews new events, they wait here. An admin must approve events.

The list shows pending items when it opens. To see flagged posts, change the status filter at the top of the list to flagged.

## Reviewing a post

1. Read the item in the list.
2. Press the approve button if it is fine. The post becomes visible to members.
3. Press the reject button if it breaks the rules. Type a **Rejection Reason** and press **Reject Content**. The post stays hidden.

The counters at the top show how many items are **Pending Review**, **Flagged**, **Approved** and **Rejected**. Press **Refresh** to update the list.

> You cannot review content you wrote yourself. Another broker or an admin must do it.

broker_feed_posts.title: Hiding or deleting feed posts
broker_feed_posts.summary: Remove posts and other items from the community feed.
broker_feed_posts.body:
[Feed Posts](/broker/moderation/feed) lists everything in your community's feed: posts, listings, events, polls and more.

## Finding an item

- Type in **Search Posts or Users...** to search by words or by the author's name.
- Use **Post Type** to show one kind of item. Press **Apply**, or **Clear** to reset.

Each row shows the author, the content, the type, whether it is **Visible** or **Hidden**, and when it was created.

## Hiding an item

Press **Hide**, then **Hide Post** to confirm. Members can no longer see it in the feed. The author gets a notification that their post was hidden. There is no button to show it again, so be sure first.

## Deleting an item

Press **Delete**, then **Delete Post** to confirm. This cannot be undone. The item leaves the feed, along with its likes and comments. The author gets a notification and an email explaining why it was removed and how to contest it.

For a listing or an event, **Delete** removes it from the feed only. The listing or event itself stays.

> You cannot hide or delete something you wrote. If a post only needs a small change, it is often kinder to message the author first.

broker_comments_reviews.title: Removing comments and reviews
broker_comments_reviews.summary: Delete comments that break the rules, and flag, hide or delete member reviews.
broker_comments_reviews.body:
## Comments

[Comments](/broker/moderation/comments) lists members' comments across the community.

1. Search with **Search Comments or Users...** and press **Apply**.
2. Find the comment.
3. To remove it, press **Delete**, then **Delete Comment** to confirm.

The comment is removed for good. The author gets a notification and an email explaining why and how to contest it.

## Reviews

If your community uses reviews, [Reviews](/broker/moderation/reviews) lists the reviews members give each other. You can search, or filter by **Rating**.

- **Flag**: takes the review off public view so it can be looked at. Nobody is notified.
- **Hide**: takes the review off public view. The member who wrote it is notified.
- **Delete**: removes the review for good. The member who wrote it is notified.

Each action asks you to confirm first. There is no button to restore a flagged or hidden review, so choose carefully.

> You cannot moderate a review you wrote, or a review about you. Ask another broker or an admin.

broker_reports.title: Dealing with members' reports
broker_reports.summary: Read reports that members make about content, then resolve or dismiss them.
broker_reports.body:
Members can report content that worries them, such as a post, comment, listing, event or review. Reports arrive in [Reports](/broker/moderation/reports). Brokers and admins get a notification when a new report arrives.

## Reading a report

1. Open [Reports](/broker/moderation/reports). The counters show **Total Reports**, **Pending**, **Resolved** and **Dismissed**.
2. Use **Status** and **Content Type** to filter, then press **Apply**.
3. Press **View details** on a report. You see who reported it, the reported item and its author, and the reason.

## Closing a report

- **Resolve**: you agree there was a problem and you have dealt with it. The person who reported it is told.
- **Dismiss**: you looked at it and no action is needed. The person who reported it gets a neutral message.

Each asks you to confirm.

## Resolving does not remove anything

Resolving or dismissing a report only closes the report. It does not change the reported content. If content should go, remove it yourself first, from **Feed Posts**, **Comments** or **Reviews**. Then resolve the report.

> You cannot close a report you made, or a report about you.

broker_group_activities.title: Workshops and group activities
broker_group_activities.summary: Record time for workshops and group sessions with group exchanges, and use a Community Pot account.

broker_group_exchange_basics.title: How group exchanges work
broker_group_exchange_basics.summary: A group exchange records time for several people at once, such as a workshop or a work day.
broker_group_exchange_basics.body:
A group exchange records one activity with several people in it. Use one for a workshop, a group work day or a class. Any member can set one up, including you.

## Who takes part

Everyone in a group exchange has one of two roles:

- **Provider**: gives time and earns hours
- **Receiver**: receives time and gives hours

The hours given by all receivers must equal the hours earned by all providers.

## How the hours are shared

When you create it, you choose a **Split Type**:

- **Equal Split**: the **Total Hours** are shared equally among the providers, and equally among the receivers.
- **Custom Hours**: you set the hours for each person yourself.
- **Weighted Split**: you give each person a weight, and hours are shared in proportion.

## The steps

1. The organiser creates it. It starts as a **Draft**.
2. The organiser presses **Start Exchange**. Everyone is asked to confirm.
3. Each participant signs in and presses **Confirm My Hours**.
4. When everyone has confirmed, the organiser presses **Complete Exchange**.

On completion, all balances move at the same moment. If any part fails, for example a receiver does not have enough hours, nothing moves at all.

## Changes

If the organiser changes the exchange after it starts, everyone's confirmations are cleared. Everyone must confirm again. This protects people from agreeing to one thing and being charged for another.

> Group exchanges do not need a broker's approval.

broker_create_group_exchange.title: Setting up a group exchange for a workshop
broker_create_group_exchange.summary: Step by step: create a group exchange, add participants and choose how hours are shared.
broker_create_group_exchange.body:
You can organise a group exchange for a group, even if you are not taking part yourself.

1. Go to [Group Exchanges](/group-exchanges) on the member side of the site. Press **Back to Site** if you are in the Broker Panel.
2. Press **New Exchange**.
3. **Details**: enter a **Title**, such as "Bike repair workshop, 12 June", and a **Description (optional)**. Enter the **Total Hours** and choose a **Split Type**. Press **Next**.
4. **Participants**: search for members and add each one as a **Provider** or a **Receiver**. If you are taking part, use **Add yourself as**. You need at least one provider and one receiver. With **Custom Hours**, enter each person's hours. Press **Next**.
5. **Review Split**: check the **Hour Split Preview**. It shows who gives, who receives and how many hours. Press **Back** to fix anything, or **Review** to go on.
6. **Confirm**: check everything and press **Create Group Exchange**.

## After you create it

1. Open the exchange and press **Start Exchange**. Participants get a notification asking them to confirm.
2. Help anyone who is unsure how to press **Confirm My Hours**.
3. When everyone shows as **Confirmed**, press **Complete Exchange**.

## Tips

- Check every receiver has enough hours before you start. One short balance stops the whole exchange.
- Every participant must confirm from their own account. Plan time for this, especially with large groups.
- If the activity is cancelled, press **Cancel Exchange**. No hours move.

broker_community_pot.title: Using a Community Pot account for workshops
broker_community_pot.summary: A Community Pot is an ordinary member account that holds hours for the whole community. Two ways to use it.
broker_community_pot.body:
Some timebanks keep a shared account for the whole community, often called a Community Pot. It is an ordinary member account. It is not a special feature of the site.

Ask your admin to create the account and agree who looks after it. That person signs in to the pot account to confirm its part in exchanges.

## Option A: attendees contribute

Each attendee gives an hour, which pays the leader and tops up the pot.

Example: a workshop with a leader and 50 attendees.

1. Create a group exchange with **Custom Hours**.
2. Add the leader as a **Provider** with 1 hour.
3. Add the Community Pot as a **Provider** with 49 hours.
4. Add each of the 50 attendees as a **Receiver** with 1 hour.

In total, 50 hours are given and 50 are earned. Each attendee needs at least 1 hour in their balance.

## Option B: the pot pays

The pot pays the leader, and attendees take part for free.

1. Create a group exchange with **Custom Hours**.
2. Add the leader as a **Provider** with 1 hour.
3. Add the Community Pot as a **Receiver** with 1 hour.

The pot needs at least 1 hour in its balance.

## Keep it fair and open

- Agree with your community when the pot pays and when attendees pay.
- Keep a note of what came in and went out.
- Members can give hours to the shared **Community Fund** from their wallet. Only an admin can pay hours out of that fund. The Community Fund and a Community Pot account are separate things.
- If your community gives hours for attending events, an admin sets the reward on each event. Brokers cannot set it.

broker_reports.title: Figures and records
broker_reports.summary: See how new members are getting on, and find the counts and records the Broker Panel keeps.

broker_onboarding_funnel.title: Seeing how new members are getting on
broker_onboarding_funnel.summary: The Onboarding page shows how far new members get, from registering to their first exchange.
broker_onboarding_funnel.body:
[Onboarding](/broker/onboarding) shows how new members are getting on. It helps you see where people get stuck, so you can offer help.

## The counters

- **Registered**: how many people have signed up, compared with last month
- **Overall conversion**: the share of registered people who reached the last step, **Repeat User**
- **Pending approvals**: people waiting for approval
- **Biggest drop-off**: the step where most people stop

## The Onboarding Funnel

The funnel shows how many members reached each step:

1. **Registered**
2. **Email Verified**
3. **Profile Complete**
4. **First Listing**
5. **First Exchange**
6. **Repeat User**

A big drop between two steps shows where people need help. For example, many people who verify their email but never complete their profile may need a welcome call.

## Registrations Trend

This chart shows new registrations each month for the last six months.

## Pending Approvals

At the bottom is the list of people waiting for approval. Use the three-dot menu on a row to **Approve** them or **View Profile**.

broker_figures_and_records.title: What figures and records can brokers see?
broker_figures_and_records.summary: Where to find counts, activity history and permanent records in the Broker Panel.
broker_figures_and_records.body:
The Broker Panel shows counts and records to help you plan your work. It does not have downloads or exports. If you need a report for funders or your committee, ask your admin.

## Counts

- The [Broker Dashboard](/broker) shows what is waiting across the whole panel.
- Most pages have counters at the top. For example, [Members](/broker/members) shows **Total members**, **Pending approval**, **Active members** and **Suspended members**.
- [Onboarding](/broker/onboarding) shows how new members progress and how many register each month.
- The red numbers in the menu show waiting work, updated about once a minute.

## Activity history

**Recent Activity** on the dashboard lists recent broker actions: who approved, reviewed, tagged or changed what, and when.

## Permanent records

- [Review Archive](/broker/archives): read-only records of message reviews
- Member notes: on each member's record
- Exchange **History**: on each exchange page
- Vetting decisions: in [Vetting confirmations](/broker/vetting)

## Figures that could not load

If a counter shows a dash, or you see **Some metrics couldn't be loaded**, press **Refresh**. A dash means the number could not be loaded. It does not mean zero.

broker_good_practice.title: Good practice for brokers
broker_good_practice.summary: Simple habits that keep your timebank fair, safe, friendly and well run.

broker_daily_routine.title: A simple daily routine for brokers
broker_daily_routine.summary: A short checklist to keep on top of the work without missing anything urgent.
broker_daily_routine.body:
A few minutes each day keeps members safe and stops work piling up. This is a suggested routine. Adapt it to your community.

1. Open the [Broker Dashboard](/broker) and read **What needs you now**.
2. Deal with safeguarding first. Check **Safeguarding Alerts**, then flagged and unreviewed items in [Messages](/broker/messages).
3. Check your notifications for coordinator help requests. Reply to each one.
4. Approve or reject exchanges waiting in [Exchanges](/broker/exchanges). Members cannot start until you do.
5. Approve new members waiting in [Members](/broker/members).
6. Check [Reports](/broker/moderation/reports) and the [Content Queue](/broker/moderation/queue).
7. Answer vetting review requests in [Vetting confirmations](/broker/vetting).
8. Skim **Recent Activity** to see what other brokers have done.

## Weekly

- Look at [User Monitoring](/broker/monitoring). Decide whether each member still needs it, especially those in **Expiring within 7 days**.
- Look at the **Never logged in** and **Onboarding incomplete** tabs in [Members](/broker/members). Offer help.
- Check [Insurance](/broker/insurance) for certificates that are **Expiring Soon**.

## Sharing the work

If several brokers share the work, agree who covers which days. Use member notes so everyone knows what has been done.

broker_fair_exchanges.title: Helping members exchange time fairly
broker_fair_exchanges.summary: Good habits that make exchanges clear and fair for everyone.
broker_fair_exchanges.body:
Timebanking works because everyone's time is valued equally. One hour of help is worth one hour, whatever the task. Here is how you can help members keep exchanges fair.

## Before an exchange

- Encourage members to agree clearly what will be done, when and roughly how long it will take.
- Suggest they use messages on the site to agree details. This keeps a record.
- Remind members that nobody has to accept a request they are not comfortable with.

## After an exchange

- Encourage both members to confirm the hours promptly.
- If they disagree, help them talk it through calmly. Most disagreements are misunderstandings.

## Being fair as a broker

- Apply the same rules to everyone.
- Do not handle exchanges, reports or corrections that involve you, a relative or a close friend. Ask another broker.
- Explain your decisions in plain words, especially when you reject something.
- Keep corrections to balances rare, agreed and explained.

## Encouraging everyone to take part

Some members find it easier to give than to ask. Remind people that receiving help is part of timebanking too. Some members may need help to think of what they can offer. Everyone has something to give.

broker_safe_exchanges.title: Helping members stay safe
broker_safe_exchanges.summary: Practical safety advice for members, and the tools brokers can use when an exchange carries more risk.
broker_safe_exchanges.body:
Most exchanges are simple and safe. A little planning helps keep them that way.

## Advice to share with members

- Meet somewhere public for a first meeting, or have someone else there.
- Tell a friend or family member where you are going and when you expect to be back.
- Keep money, bank cards and passwords out of exchanges.
- Trust your feelings. It is fine to say no, or to stop an exchange that feels wrong.
- Tell a broker if anything worries you.

## Extra care for some activities

Some activities carry more risk. Examples are visiting someone's home, driving, work with tools, or support for someone who may be at risk. For these:

- Tag the listing in [Risk Tags](/broker/risk-tags) and consider **Broker approval required**.
- Ask for insurance with **Insurance required** where your community's rules say so.
- Record vetting decisions for members who work with people at risk.
- Consider arranging the first meeting yourself.

## Protected members

Some members have asked for extra protection. Respect their choices, even if it makes arranging help slower. Never pass on their contact details without their agreement.

> If you think someone is in danger, contact the emergency services first.

broker_privacy_records.title: Keeping members' information private
broker_privacy_records.summary: How to handle what you see as a broker, and how to keep good records.
broker_privacy_records.body:
As a broker you see information other members do not: notes, safeguarding choices, vetting decisions and some messages. Members trust you with it.

## Handling information

- Look only at what you need for the task in front of you.
- Do not discuss members with other members.
- Share concerns only with other brokers, your admin or your safeguarding lead, and only as needed.
- Do not copy information out of the site into personal notes, email or chat apps.
- Sign out when you finish, especially on a shared computer.

## Keeping good records

- Write notes as facts: what happened, when, and what you did.
- Leave out opinions and guesses.
- Write each note as if the member might one day read it. They may have the right to ask for the information held about them.
- Give clear reasons when you reject, suspend, monitor or adjust a balance. These reasons stay on record.

## What not to record

- Vetting certificates, certificate numbers or check results
- Health details, unless your community's rules say you may and it is needed
- Passwords or bank details, ever

> If you think information has been seen by someone who should not see it, tell your admin straight away.

broker_welcoming_members.title: Welcoming new members
broker_welcoming_members.summary: A warm start helps new members make their first exchange.
broker_welcoming_members.body:
The first few weeks decide whether a new member stays. A friendly broker makes a big difference.

## When you approve someone

- Approve new members promptly. People lose interest if they wait.
- Send a short welcome message. Press **Send Message** from their row in [Members](/broker/members).
- Offer a phone call or a meeting if they would like help getting started.

## Helping them take their first step

- Help them add a clear profile and one or two listings: something they can offer and something they would like.
- Suggest a simple first exchange with a friendly, experienced member.
- Tell them how hours work: one hour given earns one hour to spend.

## Following up

- Use [Onboarding](/broker/onboarding) to see where new members get stuck.
- Check the **Onboarding incomplete** and **Never logged in** tabs in [Members](/broker/members) every week.
- Add a note with the category **Onboarding** when you contact someone, so other brokers know.

> Do not rush people. Some members take a while to feel confident. A kind word often matters more than any feature.
